# `.opchain/qa.yaml` — the QA manifest format

Written by `/oc-qa pyramid`, `/oc-qa coverage`, `/oc-qa contracts`, and
`/oc-qa loadplan`. Read by oc-bug-check (budgets, at its test check, **when
present** — absent file means downstream behavior is exactly pre-v1.9), by
oc-app-architect's Phase 6 Evaluator (new-code expectation), by oc-scale-ops
(the `load_plan:` block it executes), and by `/oc-qa audit` (as its own
ground truth).

Reviewed like code: the manifest lives in the repo, changes ride PRs.

## Full example

```yaml
# .opchain/qa.yaml — generated by oc-qa-ops, hand-editable
version: 1
generated: 2026-08-28
pyramid:
  levels:
    - name: unit
      belongs: "Pure logic: handlers, libs, parsers. No I/O, no network."
      excluded: "Anything needing a running server or real store."
      gate: commit            # commit | ci | nightly
      target_runtime: "30s"
    - name: integration
      belongs: "Route wiring, store adapters against local/miniflare bindings."
      excluded: "Third-party network calls (mock at the boundary)."
      gate: ci
      target_runtime: "3m"
    - name: contract
      belongs: "Cross-boundary shapes — see contracts below."
      excluded: "Behavior behind the boundary (that's unit/integration)."
      gate: ci
      target_runtime: "1m"
    - name: e2e
      belongs: "Smoke flows a user would notice breaking. Sparingly."
      excluded: "Anything a unit test already asserts."
      gate: ci
      target_runtime: "5m"
  anti_patterns:
    - "Snapshot tests of volatile rendered output"
    - "e2e restating unit assertions"
    - "Mocking code this repo owns"
coverage:
  global: { lines: 70, branches: 60 }     # floor — never above measured reality
  new_code: { lines: 80 }                 # what the build-loop Evaluator holds sprints to
  enforce: warn                           # warn (default) | fail — see field rules
  overrides:
    - { path: "src/lib/", lines: 90 }
    - { path: "scripts/", exempt: true, reason: "operational glue, smoke-covered" }
contracts:
  - boundary: "worker API <-> site fetch clients"
    artifact: "src/lib/schemas.js"
    tests: "tests/feedback.test.js"
    owner: in-repo            # in-repo | oc-api-dev | oc-integrations-engineer | oc-data-ops
    gate: ci
    drift_signal: "schema change without matching test change"
load_plan:
  handed_to: oc-scale-ops
  target: staging             # staging | production | <base url> — required;
                              #   execution cannot infer the environment
  scenarios:
    - { name: steady, endpoint: "/api/health", rps: 50, duration: "5m", slo_p95_ms: 200 }
    - { name: spike, endpoint: "/mcp", rps: 200, duration: "2m", slo_p95_ms: 500 }
    - { name: soak, endpoint: "/api/health", rps: 20, duration: "1h", slo_p95_ms: 250 }
```

## Field rules

- `pyramid.levels[].gate` must name a gate that actually runs in the repo
  (commit = oc-bug-check; ci = the PR workflow; nightly = a scheduled job).
  Declaring a gate that doesn't exist is a `/oc-qa audit` GAP finding (the
  audit checks gate wiring explicitly).
- `coverage.global` starts at measured reality. Ratchet in later PRs.
- `coverage.new_code` is advisory to humans, binding to the oc-app-architect
  Evaluator (it grades sprint test requirements against it).
- `contracts[].artifact` points at the thing both sides agree on — a schema
  file, an OpenAPI doc, a data contract (`oc-data-ops` owns those files;
  this manifest only references them).
- `contracts[].owner` records who authors the tests: `in-repo` by default;
  `oc-api-dev` rows are authored by its conformance suite (never re-authored
  here), `oc-integrations-engineer` for consumed third-party boundaries,
  `oc-data-ops` for data contracts.
- `load_plan` is a handoff, not a promise: oc-scale-ops executes and owns
  perf budgets. Every scenario needs an SLO and a `duration`, and the plan
  needs a `target` environment, or oc-qa-ops refuses to emit it.
- `coverage.enforce`: `warn` (default) or `fail`. `fail` flips a
  `coverage.global` miss from WARN to FAIL at oc-bug-check's gate — the one
  field here that changes gate semantics, which is why it is set by a human
  edit, never emitted by `/oc-qa coverage`.

## Consumption contract (downstream gates)

oc-bug-check, at its test-suite check, when `.opchain/qa.yaml` exists:

- Runs the suite exactly as before (its PASS/FAIL semantics are unchanged).
- Additionally compares coverage output (when the runner emits it) against
  `coverage.global`; a miss is reported as **WARN** — unless
  `coverage.enforce: fail` is set (a human edit), in which case the miss is
  FAIL and oc-bug-check's normal bypass protocol applies.
- An unparseable manifest, or a `version` the consumer doesn't recognize, is
  treated exactly as absent plus one WARN line ("qa.yaml unreadable — budgets
  not applied; run /oc-qa status"). Never FAIL, never block, on a manifest
  parse problem.
- A valid manifest with no `coverage:` block applies no coverage budget and
  emits nothing about coverage (the suite still runs as before).

This keeps the edge additive: no manifest, no change; manifest present,
strategy becomes visible at the gate without redefining it.
